evidence.claim: The leaders reaffirmed maintaining peace, security, stability, safety, and freedom of navigation and overflight in the South China Sea, peaceful resolution of disputes without threat or force, and substantive negotiations toward an effective Code of Conduct under UNCLOS.
evidence.title: Joint Press Statement between the Republic of the Philippines and the Republic of Singapore on Strengthening the Philippines-Singapore Partnership
evidence.excerpt: The leaders reaffirmed maintaining peace, security, stability, safety, and freedom of navigation and overflight in the South China Sea, peaceful resolution of disputes without threat or force, and substantive negotiations toward an effective Code of Conduct under UNCLOS.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary joint statement issued by a foreign ministry with dated, explicit language.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Joint leader statement that includes Marcos's administration; useful for his diplomatic posture, not battlefield conduct.
contrary_evidence: A joint statement is declaratory and does not by itself prove implementation or durable de-escalation.

evidence.claim: Biden and Marcos underscored support for freedom of navigation and overflight and the peaceful resolution of disputes in the South China Sea.
evidence.title: Biden, Marcos discuss tensions in South China Sea
evidence.excerpt: Biden and Marcos underscored support for freedom of navigation and overflight and the peaceful resolution of disputes in the South China Sea.
evidence.source_locator: article lead and White House statement quoted in the report
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent Reuters-based reporting quoting the White House statement.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to Marcos's first face-to-face talks with Biden as president.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Marcos participated directly in the bilateral meeting; the claim supports his diplomatic alignment, not proxy conduct.
contrary_evidence: Alliance strengthening can also be read as strategic balancing against China, not as an achieved peace settlement.

evidence.claim: Marcos urged continued dialogue, maximum restraint, and peaceful resolution of the Taiwan Strait, Korean Peninsula, and Russia-Ukraine crises.
evidence.title: PBBM calls for peace to end Taiwan, Korean, Russia-Ukraine crises
evidence.excerpt: Marcos urged continued dialogue, maximum restraint, and peaceful resolution of the Taiwan Strait, Korean Peninsula, and Russia-Ukraine crises.
evidence.source_locator: article body and Asia Society remarks excerpt
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government newswire reporting a dated presidential speech with direct quotation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Marcos statement in office, though on regional conflicts rather than Philippine force use.
contrary_evidence: This is exhortation, not a negotiated settlement or operational crisis intervention.

evidence.claim: Marcos said there was no new progress on the South China Sea code of conduct, but he still described the COC as necessary to keep the peace, said Taiwan should be resolved peacefully, and argued for engagement on Myanmar.
evidence.title: No progress made on 'code of conduct' at summits - Marcos
evidence.excerpt: Marcos said there was no new progress on the South China Sea code of conduct, but he still described the COC as necessary to keep the peace, said Taiwan should be resolved peacefully, and argued for engagement on Myanmar.
evidence.source_locator: article body and quoted post-summit briefing
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent report of a presidential debrief with direct quotations.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 after the ASEAN summits.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Marcos post-summit remarks in office.
contrary_evidence: It confirms process without outcome; the lack of progress limits any claim of successful restraint.

evidence.claim: Marcos and Xi agreed on the importance of an early conclusion of negotiations for a final and binding Code of Conduct in the South China Sea and said the issue should not define the whole bilateral relationship.
evidence.title: Marcos, Xi seek early conclusion of negotiations for COC in SCS
evidence.excerpt: Marcos and Xi agreed on the importance of an early conclusion of negotiations for a final and binding Code of Conduct in the South China Sea and said the issue should not define the whole bilateral relationship.
evidence.source_locator: article body and DFA summary of the Bangkok meeting
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government newswire summarizing a bilateral leader meeting and DFA release.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022, during Marcos's bilateral diplomacy with China.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Marcos meeting with Xi; this is the clearest ruler-attributed 2022 de-escalation item.
contrary_evidence: The meeting did not produce a finalized code of conduct in 2022.

evidence.claim: Marcos said the Philippines must find a way to explore oil and gas in the South China Sea even without a deal with China, and that other ways should be tried if government-to-government talks fail.
evidence.title: Philippines needs to find ways to exploit South China Sea resources, says Marcos
evidence.excerpt: Marcos said the Philippines must find a way to explore oil and gas in the South China Sea even without a deal with China, and that other ways should be tried if government-to-government talks fail.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-origin report carried by Euronews with direct quotes and dated context.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and at the end of the year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Marcos statement in office; it shows a mix of assertiveness and negotiation rather than force.
contrary_evidence: The language is more assertive than purely conciliatory and did not resolve the dispute in 2022.

unresolved_gaps: No direct nuclear-command or crisis-use decision in 2022.
No external war or proxy-conflict record in 2022, so some conduct lenses are structurally thin.
Direct chain-of-command evidence for red-tagging and some police outcomes remains limited.
Election-year evidence is stronger on campaign behavior and information environment than on post-inauguration institutional change.
National household/distribution outcomes are better evidenced in 2023 follow-through than in clean 2022-only attribution.
Most welfare evidence is rollout or partner-supported evidence rather than a full national outcome audit.
Direct 2022 asset/SALN and office-period wealth evidence remains thin.
Agency-level execution evidence is thinner than agenda-setting and budget evidence.
